newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: U.S. halts imports of Dutch pork products.
newsitem.headline: U.S. halts imports of Dutch pork products.

text.p: The U.S. has halted imports of Dutch pork products following an outbreak of swine fever in the Netherlands, the Dutch Farm Ministry said on Tuesday.
A ministry spokesman said Washington had removed the Netherlands from a list of countries which were free of swine fever and halted import of pork products.
The spokesman said the U.S. did not import any live pigs or unprocessed pork and was only a small importer of pork products.
On Monday the Dutch Farm Ministry extended an export ban on pigs which have passed through the region infected with swine fever after January 1, 1997.
Swine fever broke out in the North Brabant province of the southern Netherlands last week, prompting the Ministry to ban the export of pigs from farms in the affected region.

The Dutch authorities, anxious to prevent restrictions on key pork exports, have decided to slaughter all pigs at 26 farms in the area immediately surrounding the first farm unit to be affected. An estimated 30,000 animals are expected to be killed.
The Netherlands exports around 750,000 tonnes of pigs and pork products each year.
On Friday Poland closed its borders to all imports of Dutch pigs, pork and pork products, and Belgium said it would tighten frontier checks, although it stopped short of an outright ban.
